A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RestoreGrad, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D. The retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original speech and image restoration experiments, learning curves, ablations, and OOD and ASR evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds longer-training image results, encoder-size measurements, and sampling and diffusion-process examples.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same conditional DDPM, Prior Net and Posterior Net, Gaussian covariance learning, LR/DM/PM losses, and Algorithms 1–2. Expanded explanations and additional encoder-size experiments do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets and tasks remain unchanged, including speech enhancement, weather restoration, RealBlur deblurring, DIV2K super-resolution, and ASR evaluation. CHiME-3 and realistic-image evaluations already appear in v2 Appendix D.1; v3 moves them into Section 4.3.

E2.justification: v3 adds DTPM (Ye et al., 2024) to the weather-specific comparisons in Table 4 and RDDM (Liu et al., 2024) to the RainDrop comparison in Table 10. Existing comparators remain; these are limited additions to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 1,551-epoch AllWeather evaluation alongside the retained 887-epoch results and an image encoder-size comparison. Appendix C.3.1 also revises the stated snow evaluation from the full 50,000-image test set to Snow100K-L. Table 4 already identifies Snow100K-L in both versions, so this wording correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix D.2 adds image restoration examples across sampling seeds, an image encoder size versus quality/cost analysis, and diffusion-process snapshots (Figures 13–14 and Table 12). These supplement the retained posterior-removal, sampling-step, regularization, and speech encoder analyses.

E5.justification: The new Figure 13 analysis explicitly reports sampling seeds 1, 10, and 20. Both versions retain mean±standard-deviation reporting from 10 independent samplings in Tables 1 and 10; no increase in those repeat counts or new significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores are retained, while v3 adds comparator, longer-training, encoder-size, and qualitative results. In Table 4, the new 1,551-epoch row reports Snow100K-L PSNR 31.16 versus 30.82 at 887 epochs, but Outdoor-Rain PSNR is 30.70 versus 30.83. Table 10 adds RDDM's SSIM of 0.9563, exceeding RestoreGrad's retained 0.9441. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The background variance-schedule domain changes from β_t in [0,1) to (0,1), excluding zero. This is a limited mathematical assumption correction. Propositions 3.1–3.2 and their appendix proofs otherwise retain their substantive mathematics; loss notation and explanations are refined.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: jointly learned diffusion priors through a two-encoder VAE/DDPM framework for signal restoration. The headline claims of 5–10 times fewer training steps and 2–2.5 times fewer sampling steps remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 motivates the zero-mean modeling choice through signal normalization and extends the quality-versus-complexity interpretation to images. It interprets new intermediate-image examples as evidence of a better diffusion trajectory and reframes RainDrop performance as competitive with RDDM. The restoration-only and Gaussian covariance-only limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents the new 1.9M-parameter image encoder comparison and its V100 measurements, and clarifies that the RainDropDiff example uses weights trained by the authors. Conversely, Table 2 replaces absolute speech latency and memory measurements with ratios, removing some resource detail. Existing implementation recipes and code/data access information largely remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds the DTPM and RDDM papers and He et al.'s 2025 low-level-vision diffusion survey. It positions RestoreGrad against these newer restoration methods, including discussing DTPM's separate pretraining requirement. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted prose edits, introduces numbered background and training/sampling subsections, moves the OOD discussion from Appendix D.1 to Section 4.3, and adds publication information and an Impact Statement. The overall argument and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 13–14 and the image complexity Table 12, expands Tables 4 and 10, and simplifies Table 2 to percentage overheads. Tables 5–6 move into the main text. All original figure graphics are retained, with later examples reordered or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The newer image comparators and targeted encoder, sampling, and diffusion-process analyses modestly strengthen the evidence and clarify performance boundaries, including RDDM's higher SSIM. Reorganization also makes existing OOD evidence easier to find. These gains outweigh limited drawbacks: absolute speech resource measurements disappear, and the longer-training discussion overlooks the Outdoor-Rain PSNR decrease in Table 4. The core method and principal results remain stable.
